name: coopetition-gym-logs
description: Per-cell training, evaluation, behavioral-audit, and learning-rate-ablation results for the Coopetition-Gym v1 benchmark. The dataset comprises (i) 17,930 training-run records (16 algorithms x 20 environments x 3 reward modes x 7-10 seeds), (ii) 1,116 behavioral-audit records (1,056 static response-surface cells + 60 temporal-deviation cells), (iii) the Tier-1.5 two-dimensional SLCD sensitivity sweep (3,062 records across IPPO/ISAC/MADDPG/MASAC + Stage-C scipy calibration polish), (iv) 135 LR-ablation records (3 DDPG-family algorithms x 3 reward modes x 3 critic learning rates x 5 seeds on ApacheProject-v0), and (v) 4 calibrated case-study records (Samsung-Sony LCD, Renault-Nissan Alliance, Apache HTTP Server, Apple iOS App Store). Each per-cell record contains seed-aggregated metrics, evaluation traces, and the per-step training-return time series. The dataset accompanies the NeurIPS 2026 E&D submission 'Reward-Type Ablation Reveals Mechanism-Dependent Algorithm Rankings in Mixed-Motive Multi-Agent Evaluation'.

rai:dataCollection: All records were generated by computational simulation. Reinforcement learning agents implemented on top of Stable-Baselines3 (v2.x) and PyTorch (v2.x) were trained on Coopetition-Gym environments deployed on cloud NVIDIA RTX 5090 GPU infrastructure. Each run is deterministic given the reported seed; running the code from the companion GitHub repository with matching parameters reproduces the same results up to floating-point tolerances. No human subjects, no web scraping, no third-party data.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: None. The dataset contains no human data, no personally identifiable information, no sensitive demographic attributes, no behavioral traces of real users, and no web-scraped or otherwise scraped content. All trajectories are generated by reinforcement learning agents in synthetic environments parameterized from published business case studies (Samsung-Sony S-LCD joint venture, Renault-Nissan Alliance, Apache HTTP Server, Apple iOS App Store); the calibration metadata uses publicly documented business decisions, not individual-level information.
rai:dataBiases: Algorithm selection bias: the 18 algorithms and 101 constant-action baselines evaluated are a curated subset of multi-agent RL methods; reported rankings reflect performance of this subset under default hyperparameters and may not generalize to alternative configurations. Network capacity sensitivity is characterized in Appendix B of the companion paper. Seed sampling bias: training seeds are drawn from a uniform integer sequence; the 10-seed per-cell sampling may not exhaustively characterize the tail distribution for algorithms with known variance issues (MASAC). Environment specificity: the four case-study calibrations are historically grounded but each represents a single documented coopetitive relationship; findings may not generalize to un-calibrated coopetitive settings. Parameter-coverage bias: claims in the accompanying paper that rely on observed floors or independences are characterized across at least three parameter values where feasible; the 2D SLCD sweep extends this to a 5x5 grid in two parameters.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended uses: (a) independent verification of algorithm rankings and reward-ablation findings reported in the companion paper; (b) post-hoc secondary analysis studying training-return distributions, failure modes, or alternative evaluation methodologies for mixed-motive multi-agent settings; (c) reference dataset for methodology papers that examine benchmark-variance characterization. Out-of-scope uses: the dataset is NOT intended to train RL agents directly (files contain metric summaries, not trajectory data); it is NOT a labeled dataset for supervised learning; and it should NOT be used as production training input for downstream automated decision systems in actual business settings without extensive additional validation.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset contains only result summaries (metrics, seeds, training time, final trust and appropriation levels), not full trajectories. Reconstructing intermediate policy state or step-by-step observations requires re-running the training code from the companion GitHub repository. The 10-seed extension (seeds 99-108) was completed in April 2026; earlier releases of the same study used a 7-seed baseline (seeds 99-105), and that earlier baseline is not included here.
rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 (each record is a single computed evaluation summary per run)
rai:annotationDemographics: Not applicable; no human annotators were involved. Each record is a deterministic function of the algorithm, environment, and seed.

distribution.name: huggingface_repository
distribution.description: HuggingFace dataset repository (git remote). The validator's record-generation test attempts a full git clone of this remote to enumerate the JSONL shards. Anonymous git clone is permitted by HuggingFace for this public dataset; if the validator container does not have outbound git access or hits its sandbox timeout during the ~1.6 GB clone, the test will report 'Could not automatically generate records' which the NeurIPS Croissant Validator documents as non-blocking for submission. The dataset itself is fully accessible at https://huggingface.co/datasets/vikpant/coopetition-gym-logs and its files can be fetched individually via the HF resolve API.

distribution.name: lr_ablation
distribution.description: Learning-rate ablation: 3 DDPG-family algorithms (MADDPG, MATD3, M3DDPG) x 3 reward modes (private, integrated, cooperative) x 3 critic learning rates (1e-3, 1e-4, 1e-5) x 5 seeds (99-103) on ApacheProject-v0 = 135 records. recordSet.name: behavioral_audit_records
recordSet.description: Static action-audit and temporal-audit results characterizing the geometric properties of environment payoff landscapes. 1,056 action-audit files (18 policies × 20 environments × 3 seeds, minus 24 degenerate MeanFieldAC dyadic runs) sweep uniform cooperation from 0% to 100% and test unilateral deviation at four levels; 60 temporal-audit files test accumulate-then-defect strategies via binary switchpoints and gradual ramp-down. Result: exploitation gradient is bounded (binary switchpoints universally blocked; gradual ramp-down yields at most +0.41% of baseline return on 6 environments).

recordSet.name: case_study_calibration_records
recordSet.description: Four validated case-study calibrations: Samsung-Sony SLCD (98.3% = 59/60), Renault-Nissan Alliance (81.7% = 49/60), Apache HTTP Server (86.7% = 52/60), and Apple iOS App Store (87.3% = 48/55). recordSet.name: tier_1_5_2d_slcd_records
recordSet.description: Tier-1.5 sensitivity-sweep results on a two-dimensional extension of the Samsung-Sony SLCD environment where each agent chooses (c_i, p_i) = (cooperation, appropriation). Three-stage study: Stage A sweeps IPPO and ISAC over a η×β grid (η ∈ {0.20, 0.30, 0.40, 0.50, 0.60}, β ∈ {0.30, 0.60, 0.75, 0.90}) × 30 seeds = 1,500 runs per algorithm; Stage B runs MADDPG and MASAC supplementary sweeps at η=0.40, β=0.60; Stage C fits (κ, ξ) to the 'A_flat_peak' waypoint target via scipy bracket search. Finding: the β=0.90 bounce-back at η=0.40 is unimodal (Hartigan's dip test keeps H₀, p=0.88) rather than bimodal; the sensitivity sweep does not uncover a pathological attractor landscape.

rai:dataSocialImpact: Positive impact: the dataset enables independent verification of multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithm rankings across reward-mutuality configurations; supports methodology research on mixed-motive evaluation; provides a reference benchmark for studies of CTDE-versus-independent-learning advantages, training stability, and saturation regimes; and grounds claims about MARL methodology in a 19,046-experiment empirical base. Potential negative impact: the four case-study calibrations encode documented corporate partnerships (Samsung-Sony S-LCD joint venture, Renault-Nissan Alliance, Apache HTTP Server community, Apple iOS App Store platform) and could in principle be misused to optimize for partner harm in real corporate settings or to make causal-historical inferences from policy behavior in the simulator. The companion paper (Section on Societal Impact) explicitly enumerates these out-of-scope deployments and the dataset is licensed CC-BY 4.0 with the use-restrictions narrative carried in rai:dataUseCases. No personally identifiable information is present (see rai:personalSensitiveInformation).
